body.message:
VERDICT: the inventory-total answer (record 01M17FRSCNMPXN9AYWVAZZECNT) is CORRECT. Both the total and the count check out.

Independent recount. I queried kind 'note' with match {topic:'inventory'} and got exactly 4 records, no more page: widget A: 3 (01M17FP7NP0RR4EA92JAFCKW11), widget B: 11 (01M17FP7RHD2TXZ4VDFVA8V51C), widget C: 0 (01M17FP7TR9JF26AZNDCCTENHD), widget D: 6 (01M17FP7X6S2HTN7E8X03YYZ49). 3 + 11 + 0 + 6 = 20, over 4 notes. The answer says message '20', count 4. Both match.

I also read src/main.js in the 'inventory' workspace rather than trusting the number alone, so a right answer arrived at by a wrong route would still have been caught. The routine queries the same {topic:'inventory'} pattern with limit 500, pulls the first integer out of each message via /-?\d+/, sums, and reports (notes).length as the count. On this data that is the right computation, and it is a real computation rather than a hardcoded constant. Two specifics worth confirming: widget C at 0 is genuinely counted (it contributes 0 to the sum but does increment count to 4, which is why count 4 and not 3 is correct), and the limit of 500 is far above the 4 records present, so nothing was truncated.

One latent fragility, NOT a defect in this run and it does not qualify the verdict: 'first integer in the message' would take the wrong number if an item name ever contained a digit ('widget 2A: 3 in stock' would total 2). No current note has that shape, so the answer stands as correct. Flagging it only in case the inventory notes are later written by something other than a human.
